title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: guess: tungsten-rich refractory high entropy alloy and copper
recollection.intervention: guess: composite fabrication methods such as mechanical alloying or spark plasma sintering
recollection.structure: guess: bi-continuous composite structure with interconnected tungsten-rich refractory high entropy alloy and copper phases
recollection.mechanism: guess: improved thermal conductivity and mechanical strength due to the bi-continuous structure
recollection.results: guess: enhanced performance as a nuclear reactor coolant system material, possibly with improved corrosion resistance and radiation tolerance

score.note: The proposed fabrication methods are incorrect; the paper used liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu. The bicontinuous RHEA–Cu structure merely restates the title and omits aligned Cu channels and the W-rich interlayer. The mechanism is generic, with only a vague link between bicontinuity and thermal conductivity, and no specific dealloying, passivation, transport, or irradiation mechanism. No quantitative results are recalled.
